raw_text: I'm member_002 (independent reviewer). No fixed candidate has been published yet. Please publish your fixed candidate with fix_patch and notify me via handoff_patch. For my review I will integrate your exact patch, run the public tests on that exact version (sympy/simplify/tests/test_sqrtdenest.py and test_radsimp.py), and check the issue reproduction: sqrtdenest((3 - sqrt(2)*sqrt(4 + 3*I) + 3*I)/2) should return 3/2 - sqrt(2)*sqrt(4 + 3*I)/2 + 3*I/2 without raising. Please also add a regression test in the public test file so the fix is verifiable.

Final fixed candidate published as patch-1 (source v4, files_sha256 bc5f8f36...). Please integrate_patch patch-1, run the public tests on that exact version, then org_review_patch accept or request_changes.

What changed (2 files):
1. sympy/simplify/radsimp.py, split_surds:
   - surd filter was `[x[1]**2 for x in coeff_muls if x[1].is_Pow]`; now a Pow term counts as a surd only when its square is a positive rational:
     `if x[1].is_Pow and (x[1]**2).is_Rational and x[1]**2 > 0`
   - added `if not surds: return S.One, S.Zero, S.Zero` before `_split_gcd`, which was the actual IndexError site (`g = a[0]` on an empty tuple).
2. sympy/simplify/tests/test_sqrtdenest.py: new `test_issue_12420` regression asserting
   `sqrtdenest((3 - sqrt(2)*sqrt(4 + 3*I) + 3*I)/2) == S(3)/2 - sqrt(2)*sqrt(4 + 3*I)/2 + 3*I/2` and that it does not raise.

Behavioral argument: with no viable surds, _sqrt_match receives g=1, a=0, b=0, so `a < b` is False and the expression falls through and is returned unchanged — exactly the requested "return unchanged if it cannot be denested".

My own public evidence on the identical version (report test-report-f21a7be089ddf8101f152fe3, public_test_sequence 20): sympy/simplify/tests/test_radsimp.py + sympy/simplify/tests/test_sqrtdenest.py => 33 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Treat this as my private report only; please reproduce independently on the integrated patch.

Independent review recorded: ACCEPT for patch-1 (review-1), on the exact identity you published (files_sha256 bc5f8f3686a0b83126d90bba8253e87333d13d5c792e0d86a24064df85220ab6, diff_sha256 9866ae68...).

My own evidence, not your private report: I integrated patch-1 into my separate tree (no conflicts, resulting files_sha256 identical to yours) and ran the public tests on that exact version (my source v2): sympy/simplify/tests/test_radsimp.py + sympy/simplify/tests/test_sqrtdenest.py => 33 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (my report test-report-4b2a9fb8bfaf9ebf6f361fe6, public_test_sequence 27).

Independent assessment of the repair: the root cause was split_surds passing an empty surds tuple to _split_gcd, because '4 + 3*I' is not a rational square. Narrowing the surd filter to Pow terms whose square is a positive Rational plus the early neutral return (S.One, S.Zero, S.Zero) makes _sqrt_match yield a=0, b=0, r=1, so the denesters produce nothing and _sqrtdenest1 returns expr unchanged — the required "return unchanged if it cannot be denested", achieved without a broad try/except. test_issue_12420 is present and executed in the passing run; the surrounding denesting suites stay green.

No changes requested. Your next steps are yours as delivery member: integrate the accepted candidate into your final working tree, run_tests on that exact final version, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. Acceptance does not merge anything into your tree, so please re-verify on your own final version before submitting.

patch-2 is the re-publication of your already-accepted content as the fixed candidate bound to my current workspace version — no code changed.

Identity check you can verify yourself: patch-2 has files_sha256 bc5f8f3686a0b83126d90bba8253e87333d13d5c792e0d86a24064df85220ab6 and diff_sha256 9866ae6891c20d0258d53d092827a928ece285fb997b19b7345575393a461bb3 — identical to patch-1 that you integrated and accepted as review-1.

Why it exists: after your acceptance I briefly created a scratch verification script in my tree (v5), which changed my workspace identity, then deleted it (v6) restoring the exact accepted bytes. To keep the fixed candidate bound to the tree I will actually deliver, I re-published the identical content as patch-2.

My own public evidence on the exact current version v6 (test sequence 43): sympy/simplify/tests/test_sqrtdenest.py + sympy/simplify/tests/test_radsimp.py => 33 passed, 1 skipped, validation_status verified.

If you consider re-verifying unnecessary given the byte-identical identity, I understand; if you want a same-version record for patch-2, integrate_patch patch-2, run_tests on those two modules, then org_review_patch accept. Independently, in my own self-review the substantive points are: (1) the new surd filter only drops Pow terms whose square is not a positive Rational, which previously caused _split_gcd to receive zero items and hit g = a[0]; (2) genuine denesting is unaffected because those inputs pass positive Rational squares through to _split_gcd exactly as before; (3) the empty-guard return (S.One, S.Zero, S.Zero) is the neutral a + b*sqrt(r) with b = 0, so _sqrt_match yields no r and sqrtdenest leaves the expression unchanged rather than raising. Public evidence covers the issue expression and pre-existing denesting cases in these two modules only — not the whole suite.

ACCEPT recorded as review-2 for patch-2 (source v6, files_sha256 bc5f8f36..., diff_sha256 9866ae68...) — no changes requested. You are clear to run your final integration.

Independent verification I actually performed:
1. Deleted my earlier temporary probe file review_probe_12420.py, so my tree returned to exactly files_sha256 bc5f8f3686a0b83126d90bba8253e87333d13d5c792e0d86a24064df85220ab6 — byte-identical to your published candidate. My scratch file can never contaminate your final endpoint.
2. integrate_patch patch-2 into my private copy: 0 conflicts, tree hash bc5f8f36... (v5), matching your published files_sha256 and diff_sha256, so patch-2 is byte-identical content to patch-1.
3. Public tests on that exact v5 tree (report test-report-a657d2704483f533da9c3740, sequence 52): sympy/simplify/tests/test_radsimp.py (21) + sympy/simplify/tests/test_sqrtdenest.py (13) => 33 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed, validation_status verified.
4. Issue behavior checked against the contract, not just "tests pass": test_issue_12420 asserts exactly the issue's New Result 3/2 - sqrt(2)*sqrt(4+3*I)/2 + 3*I/2, i.e. returned unchanged. A focused run of only that test also passed (seq 45).
5. Diff and caller review: the surd filter now keeps only Pow terms whose square is a positive rational, plus `if not surds: return S.One, S.Zero, S.Zero` before _split_gcd — which directly removes the literal `g = a[0]` IndexError. No try/except swallowing. At the traceback frame _sqrt_match (sqrtdenest.py line 160), split_surds is only reached when all addends have rational squares, so the (1,0,0) sentinel is the no-denesting signal and the expression comes back unchanged.

Correction to my own earlier record: in review-1 I had flagged a worry that a zero determinant might divert into a fourth-root/_sqrt_numeric_denest branch and return a bogus value. That concern is refuted — it would have changed the output and failed test_issue_12420. The accept stands; only my stated mechanism was muddled.

For your final step: after integrating patch-2 into your own tree, run the public tests on your exact final version and then submit_integration. Tests on my version are evidence for my copy only, not for yours.
